title: MEPS 2024 full-year file supplies a newer design-based health-cost vintage
source_unit: AHRQ MEPS Household Component 2024 Full-Year Consolidated Public Use File release and 2026 release schedule

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; full-year consolidated PUF release

denominator.unit: official MEPS HC-256 public-use file release

panel_rounds.value: Rounds 3-5 of Panel 28 and Rounds 1-3 of Panel 29

release_formats.value: SAS, SPSS, Stata, R statements, ASCII, SAS transport, SAS V9, Excel, and Stata data file

downloaded_stata_rows.unit: records in locally downloaded HC-256 Stata artifact

downloaded_stata_columns.unit: variables in locally downloaded HC-256 Stata artifact

positive_person_weights.unit: records with PERWT24F greater than zero in structural scan

hc036brr_unique_person_ids.unit: unique person IDs in downloaded HC-036BRR Stata artifact

hc256_ids_found_in_hc036brr.unit: HC-256 person IDs found in HC-036BRR artifact

hc256_id_linkage_rate.unit: percent of HC-256 person IDs present in HC-036BRR

observations.method: AHRQ release and documentation pages were checked for the file identifier, calendar-year scope, panel-round coverage, and delivery formats; the structural scan is reported separately from the design-based estimate.
observations.uncertainty: The structural scan confirms artifact shape and weight-field presence, not a weighted population estimate. It does not audit all substantive universes or panel comparability. The 2024 file combines overlapping panels and requires file-specific interpretation.
observations.subgroup: The released PUF covers the civilian noninstitutionalized US population; subgroup estimates remain uncomputed in this gate.
observations.counterinterpretation: A newer file can improve recency while breaking comparability through panel composition, variable changes, weighting, coding, or revised historical definitions; release availability is not evidence of a trend.

full_year_consolidated_release.unit: scheduled August 2026 release and current file page

replicate_variance_release.value: 1996-2024 replicate file for BRR variance estimation
replicate_variance_release.unit: scheduled August 2026 release and downloaded HC-036BRR artifact

brr_person_records.unit: person records in HC-036BRR, official description

brr_sample_indicators.unit: sample indicators in HC-036BRR, official description

observations.method: AHRQ MEPS public-use release schedule checked for 2026 file timing and the separate longitudinal, full-year, and variance-file artifacts.
observations.uncertainty: A schedule is not proof that a file is downloadable, unchanged, or analytically ready; release timing, documentation, and file integrity must be rechecked at acquisition.
observations.subgroup: Future Panel 28 longitudinal and 2024 full-year users; no estimates promoted.
observations.counterinterpretation: The existence of a newer panel does not make the current Panel 27 result obsolete; it may answer a different question or have a different sample and estimand.

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; all HC-256 records with positive PERWT24F and valid expenditure field

denominator.unit: HC-256 person records with positive PERWT24F and valid measure

total_health_expenditure.unit: dollars per person in calendar year
total_health_expenditure.variance_method: standard BRR across 128 replicates; replicate weight = BRR flag * 2 * PERWT24F

self_family_payment.unit: dollars per person in calendar year
self_family_payment.variance_method: standard BRR across 128 replicates; replicate weight = BRR flag * 2 * PERWT24F

observations.method: HC-256 Stata artifact joined to HC-036BRR by DUPERSID and PANEL. Final PERWT24F was used for the point estimate; each BRR replicate used BRR1-BRR128 flag * 2 * PERWT24F. Standard BRR variance is the mean squared deviation of the 128 replicate estimates; intervals are normal-approximation 95% intervals.
observations.uncertainty: This is a descriptive person-level estimate for calendar year 2024, not a household affordability estimate or causal effect. It excludes records with nonpositive weights or missing measure values; expenditure distributions are skewed; normal intervals and standard-BRR construction do not resolve panel overlap, nonresponse, service mix, price, or need composition.
observations.subgroup: Civilian noninstitutionalized US persons represented in HC-256 with positive final person weight and valid total-expenditure/self-family-payment fields; no subgroup conditioning in this estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher or lower spending can reflect health need, prices, insurance, utilization, age, provider mix, or data composition. Self/family payment is not total household burden and does not reveal delayed care, debt, unpaid time, or recovery.

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; poverty-category subgroup estimates among HC-256 records with positive PERWT24F and valid expenditure field

denominator.unit: HC-256 person records with positive PERWT24F and valid measure; each poverty category has its own valid subgroup count

total_health_expenditure_by_poverty_cate.unit: dollars per represented person in calendar year

self_family_payment_by_poverty_category.unit: dollars per represented person in calendar year

observations.method: POVCAT24 categories were estimated separately using PERWT24F for the point estimate and BRR1-BRR128 * 2 * PERWT24F for standard-BRR replicate estimates; each subgroup mean is normalized within its poverty category.
observations.uncertainty: These are descriptive person-level subgroup means, not household affordability or causal estimates. Category cells have different valid counts, income categories may reflect health need and age as well as resources, and the normal intervals do not resolve selection, panel composition, expenditure skew, or burden outside self/family payment.
observations.subgroup: POVCAT24: poor/negative, near poor, low income, middle income, and high income; category labels follow the HC-256 value labels.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher self/family payment in higher-income categories may reflect greater utilization, age, insurance mix, provider use, or ability to purchase care rather than greater financial hardship. Lower direct payment in poorer categories does not establish lower need or lower burden.

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; full-year insurance coverage subgroup estimates among HC-256 records with positive PERWT24F and valid expenditure field

denominator.unit: HC-256 person records with positive PERWT24F and valid measure; each coverage category has its own valid subgroup count

total_health_expenditure_by_insurance_ca.unit: dollars per represented person in calendar year

self_family_payment_by_insurance_categor.unit: dollars per represented person in calendar year

observations.method: INSURC24 categories were estimated separately using PERWT24F for the point estimate and BRR1-BRR128 * 2 * PERWT24F for standard-BRR replicate estimates; each subgroup mean is normalized within its coverage category.
observations.uncertainty: These are descriptive person-level subgroup means, not coverage effects or household affordability estimates. The under-65 and 65-plus categories differ by age universe, insurance selection, health need, and provider use; categories with 66 or 15 valid records are not promoted in the reader comparison.
observations.subgroup: INSURC24: under-65 private, under-65 public only, under-65 uninsured, and selected 65-plus Medicare categories; labels follow the HC-256 value labels.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower self/family payment among publicly covered people may reflect coverage design, eligibility, health need, service use, age, or provider mix; it does not establish lower total burden, better access, or less unmet need. Higher payment among privately covered under-65 people is not a causal insurance effect.

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; HC-254G office-based medical provider event layer

denominator.unit: office-based medical provider event records associated with positive PERWT24F; person-level non-users are absent from the event file

office_visits.unit: millions of office-based provider visits; Taylor SE 78.0669 million; 95% CI 2257.0815–2563.1036

mean_total_payments_per_visit.unit: dollars per office-based provider event; Taylor SE 7.9482; 95% CI 292.4741–323.6309

mean_self_family_payment_per_visit.unit: dollars per office-based provider event; Taylor SE 3.0397; 95% CI 51.4199–63.3354

positive_payment_share.unit: percent of office-based provider events with OBXP24X greater than zero; Taylor SE 0.0878 percentage points

telehealth_share.unit: percent of office-based provider events flagged telehealth; Taylor SE 0.6864 percentage points

under65_private_event_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per office-based event; Taylor SE 4.6985; 95% CI 66.5428–84.9608; 62,776 valid events

under65_public_only_event_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per office-based event; Taylor SE 3.2890; 95% CI 8.3509–21.2436; 23,022 valid events

under65_uninsured_event_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per office-based event; Taylor SE 23.9247; 95% CI 70.1317–163.9167; 1,436 valid events

observations.method: HC-254G event records were restricted to positive PERWT24F and analyzed with the event file's VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization design. HC-256 INSURC24 was appended by DUPERSID and PANEL for the under-65 coverage-conditioned event means.
observations.uncertainty: The event file represents people with reported office-based visits and does not include person-level non-users; event means are not annual household burden or person prevalence. Payment variables are imputed/edited MEPS expenditure fields, and coverage-conditioned event comparisons reflect age, need, utilization, provider type, and selection as well as coverage.
observations.subgroup: National positive-weight office-based provider events; under-65 private, under-65 public-only, and under-65 uninsured event strata appended from INSURC24.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower public-only payment per office visit may reflect coverage payment design or different services and health needs, while the uninsured estimate is imprecise and may reflect payment avoidance, delayed care, or provider/payment composition. A positive-payment event is not proof that a household experienced no financial stress.

under65_private_purchase_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per prescribed-medicine purchase; Taylor SE 2.3757; 95% CI 17.1702–26.4829; 62,035 valid purchases

under65_public_only_purchase_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per prescribed-medicine purchase; Taylor SE 0.5983; 95% CI 2.9500–5.2953; 40,300 valid purchases

under65_uninsured_purchase_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per prescribed-medicine purchase; Taylor SE 10.0941; 95% CI 35.2750–74.8440; 2,499 valid purchases

observations.method: HC-254A event records were restricted to positive PERWT24F and analyzed with the event file's VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization design. HC-256 INSURC24 was appended by DUPERSID and PANEL for the under-65 coverage-conditioned purchase means.
observations.uncertainty: The event file represents people with prescribed-medicine purchases and does not include person-level non-purchasers; purchase means are not annual household burden or person prevalence. Payment variables are imputed/edited MEPS expenditure fields, and coverage-conditioned comparisons reflect age, need, medication mix, utilization, and selection as well as coverage.
observations.subgroup: National positive-weight prescribed-medicine purchase events; under-65 private, under-65 public-only, and under-65 uninsured purchase strata appended from INSURC24.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower public-only payment per purchase may reflect coverage design or medication mix, while the uninsured estimate is imprecise and may reflect lower access, different medicines, or payment composition. A purchase does not show adherence, clinical necessity, financial hardship, or whether an intended medicine was never obtained.

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; HC-254E emergency-room visit event layer

emergency_room_visits.unit: millions of emergency-room visits; Taylor SE 2.2640 million; 95% CI 63.7750–72.6497

mean_self_family_payment_per_visit.unit: dollars per emergency-room visit; Taylor SE 12.7317; 95% CI 123.2684–173.1767

under65_private_er_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per emergency-room visit; Taylor SE 25.5267; 95% CI 237.0648–337.1296; 1,267 valid visits

under65_public_only_er_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per emergency-room visit; Taylor SE 6.9834; 95% CI 13.2355–40.6103; 1,173 valid visits

under65_uninsured_er_payment.unit: dollars self/family payment per emergency-room visit; Taylor SE 45.5094; 95% CI 430.3519–608.7487; 96 valid visits

observations.method: HC-254E event records were restricted to positive PERWT24F and analyzed with the event file's VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization design. Self/family payment sums facility and doctor self/family amounts. HC-256 INSURC24 was appended by DUPERSID and PANEL for the under-65 coverage-conditioned visit means.
observations.uncertainty: The event file represents people with reported emergency-room visits and does not include person-level non-users; event means are not annual household burden or person prevalence. Emergency-room payment estimates reflect severity, facility and physician components, coverage, provider mix, and selection. The uninsured subgroup is based on 96 valid visits and remains imprecise.
observations.subgroup: National positive-weight emergency-room events; under-65 private, under-65 public-only, and under-65 uninsured visit strata appended from INSURC24.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher uninsured direct payment among observed emergency-room visits may reflect acute severity, payment exposure, selection into emergency care, or billing composition; it does not show that insurance caused the difference or that people without visits had lower unmet need.

hospital_inpatient_stays.unit: millions of inpatient stays; Taylor SE 1.0874 million; 95% CI 26.2627–30.5253

mean_total_payments_per_stay.unit: dollars per inpatient stay; Taylor SE 758.9021; 95% CI 17405.2489–20380.1452

mean_self_family_payment_per_stay.unit: dollars per inpatient stay; Taylor SE 121.9083; 95% CI 626.2580–1104.1386

observations.method: HC-254D event records were restricted to positive PERWT24F and analyzed with the event file's VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization design. Self/family payment sums facility and doctor self/family amounts. HC-256 INSURC24 was appended by DUPERSID and PANEL for the under-65 coverage-conditioned stay means; the 20-event uninsured cell is not promoted.
observations.uncertainty: The event file represents people with reported inpatient stays and does not include person-level non-users; event means are not annual household burden or person prevalence. Inpatient payment reflects severity, length of stay, facility and physician components, coverage, and selection. The uninsured under-65 cell has only 20 valid stays and is excluded from the reader comparison.
observations.subgroup: National positive-weight inpatient-stay events; under-65 private and under-65 public-only stay strata appended from INSURC24.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower public-only payment per inpatient stay may reflect coverage design, severity, length of stay, service mix, or selection; it does not establish lower need or better outcomes. A recorded stay does not identify the household's debt, work loss, unpaid care, or recovery path.

related_sources.claim: HC-256 documentation describes the 2024 Full-Year Consolidated PUF and its panel/sample design boundaries.

HC-036BRR supplies 128 sample indicators and standard person IDs for constructing BRR replicate variances for HC-256 and prior MEPS person files.

AHRQ instructs analysts to merge BRR1-BRR128 by DUPERSID and PANEL, multiply each flag by 2 and the full-year person weight for standard BRR replicate weights, and compute design-based variance from the replicates.

boundary: This record promotes bounded descriptive 2024 person-level, poverty/coverage subgroup, and office-based event estimates after HC-256 structural, weight, HC-036BRR linkage, standard-BRR, and HC-254G event-design checks. It does not promote a household affordability, causal, unmet-need, delayed-care, unpaid-care, work-disruption, or prior-vintage trend claim. Those require harmonized universes, episode linkage, treatment continuity, household resources, recovery, and matched interpretation against Panel 27 and Panel 28 designs.
